docs.title: Team Introduction
docs.text:
Team 102 is developing Project Aurora as part of EGR 304: Embedded Systems Design at Arizona State University. Our team is working collaboratively to identify user needs, establish product requirements, develop design concepts, and integrate the hardware and software needed for the final embedded system.

This website documents the complete development of Project Aurora. Readers can use the navigation menu to review our team organization, user-needs research, product requirements, design ideas, system block diagram, software proposal, and supporting information in the appendices.

docs.title: Team Charter
docs.text:
Team 102 discussed the goals, responsibilities, and working expectations needed to complete Project Aurora successfully. Based on this discussion and the detailed planning recorded in the Appendix: Team Organization, the team agreed on the following charter:

Team 102 commits to designing and building Project Aurora through respectful collaboration, dependable communication, shared responsibility, and evidence-based engineering decisions. Each member will complete assigned work on time, attend and participate in team meetings, document their progress, share technical knowledge, and help resolve problems constructively. The team will hold every member accountable while ensuring that all four individual subsystems operate safely and successfully as one complete system.

This charter gives the team a shared standard for decision-making and accountability. The team’s success will be measured not only by completing the course requirements, but also by producing a functional prototype, developing practical engineering skills, and creating professional documentation that each member can include in their portfolio.

docs.title: Product Mission Statement
docs.text:
Team 102 considered the intended users, operating environment, primary function, and common failures associated with an advanced medication monitor. Based on this discussion, the team developed the following product mission statement:

Project Aurora’s mission is to support people who take daily medication by providing an reliable, easy to use, medication storage that helps organize doses, manage routine, and detects if medication is stored in the proper environment.

Project Aurora will be an advanced storage device that will include LED's for alerting user to take medication, while keeping track of interaction done by user and amount of pills taken out of storage. In addition device will include a environment sensor to ensure storage is acceptable.

The project will be divided into four modular subsystems: weight sensor, to detect if pill is taken out of bottle, cap open/close sensor to detect if pill bottle is opened, an alarm system(led,buzzer,etc) to remind user to take medication, and a temperature/light sensor to detect if medication is stored in right place.

docs.title: 5. Windtrace Automatic Pill Dispenser for Elderly with Alarm
docs.text:
• Price: $55.99
  • Vendor: Amazon.
  • Brand: Windtrace.
  • Rating: 4.0 out of 5 stars from 1,108 ratings.
  • Description: This pill dispenser has 28 compartments for organizing medication. It uses an alarm and flashing lights to remind users when it is time to take their pills. The tray rotates to the scheduled compartment, and the user opens the dispensing slot and tilts the device to get the pills out.
  • Connection to our project: This product helps us understand what people need from medication reminders and storage. The reviews show what users like and what causes problems during setup, refilling, and everyday use.

docs.title: Positive Comments
docs.text:
The following three positive comments come from two five-star reviews.

Voice of the Customer Restated Customer Need Kerry K., 5 stars, August 21, 2026: “Our son had a stroke and is unable to manage his pills without this organizer. It alarms and notifies him when to take them and also prevents taking the wrong pills at the wrong time.” 1. The device reminds users when it is time to take their medication. (Explicit) 2. The device helps users manage their medication with less help from others. (Latent) 3. The device helps caregivers worry less about missed or repeated doses. (Latent) cheryl samples, 5 stars, September 3, 2026: “They can only get the doses needed at that time. They can't take the next day by accident or because they didn't think they took it.” 4. The device helps prevent users from accidentally taking another dose. (Explicit) cheryl samples, 5 stars, September 3, 2026: “Well made perfect for what we needed. No more accidental dosing and easy to set up.” 5. The device is easy to set up and program. (Explicit)

docs.title: Negative Comments
docs.text:
Voice of the Customer Restated Customer Need Carole Hetrick, 1 star, September 7, 2026: “Very confusing to set up because the paper directions were not detailed enough.” The reviewer also said the instructions did not match the device and that helping the user was difficult without being there to see the buttons. 6. The instructions are clear and match the device being used. (Explicit) 7. The device lets users fix setup mistakes easily. (Latent) 8. The device allows caregivers to help with problems without being physically present. (Latent) A-OK, 1 star, September 9, 2023: “The alarm volume is too low, even at the highest setting.” The reviewer also described a flimsy cover latch and said the dosage-ring tabs covered pills inside the compartments. 9. The alarm is easy to hear, including for users with reduced hearing. (Explicit) 10. The dosage labels leave the pills visible and easy to reach. (Explicit) 11. The cover and locking parts hold up during normal use. (Explicit) Sissy D, 1 star, June 20, 2026: “Anyone can open it, it does not lock! The only part that locks and requires a key is the battery compartment!!” 12. The device keeps stored medication secure from unintended access. (Explicit) 13. The device makes it clear which parts are locked and what the lock protects. (Latent)

Some reviewers said the device helped prevent extra doses, while others reported problems with the lock. These are different customer experiences, so we should consider both when developing our design.

docs.title: Additional Comments
docs.text:
These reviews provide more information about refilling and getting pills out. The three-star review is used as extra feedback, rather than one of the required one- or two-star negative reviews.

Voice of the Customer Restated Customer Need Justine Frederick, 1 star, May 2, 2026: “The lid does not open wide but stays at an angle and slams shut.” The reviewer also said this made the tray difficult to remove. 14. The device gives users enough access to refill the medication easily. (Explicit) SM, 3 stars, August 13, 2026: “Works for 2 times a day dispensing.” The reviewer also said users can see when doses have been missed. 15. The device supports more than one medication time each day. (Explicit) 16. The device lets users or caregivers see when a dose has been missed. (Explicit) SM, 3 stars, August 13, 2026: The reviewer said pills sometimes get stuck and must be removed with a finger. They also mentioned that getting pills out can be difficult for people with large fingers or limited dexterity. 17. The device lets users remove the full dose without pills getting stuck. (Explicit) 18. The device is easy to use for people with limited finger movement. (Explicit) SM, 3 stars, August 13, 2026: “The paper dial in the middle has to be taped in place as it slips.” 19. The dosage labels stay in place during use. (Explicit) Based on SM's comment about using a finger to remove stuck pills: This also suggests that users need a cleaner way to get their medication out. 20. The device helps keep pills clean when users remove them. (Latent)

docs.title: Project Objective
docs.text: This project aims to investigate and develop smart adaptive technologies, an improved user experience, better fit, improved product design, and product customization options for the next-generation AirPods. The target is to maintain global dominance in the wireless earphone market, drive up AirPod sales to 100 million+ units sold with a 60% global market share in 2021 and expand the user base more towards the luxury, professional, and fitness segments. We believe that adding smart interactions and adaptive audio filters alone will already expand our user base by 15%. With the new generation AirPods we aim to match at least the sound quality of our main competitor, the Sony WF-1000XM3, and include Active Noise Canceling that is also featured in Mifo, House of Marley, Bose, and Amazon Echo products. We will also obtain IPX4 sweat-resistant rating equal to Bose, House of Marley, and Amazon Echo earbuds, and aim to extend our range of colors, as seen in Urbanista and Jabra’s lifestyle products.

docs.title: Stakeholders
docs.text:
• Target group High-income upper-class professionals between the age of 20 and 45. Their personalities are determined and ambitious. The main benefits sought are recreation and self-expression.
  • Target purchaser Target group profile with special attention to Full Nest I and Full Nest II mothers.
  • Customer service Prefers easy-to-repair, recyclable product, and easy-to-fix complaints to fit with Apple’s intuitive user experience.
  • Marketing & Sales division Looks for unique selling points around the Apple Aspirer-Explorer lifestyle and user experience.
  • Retailers Prefer products that can withstand a wide range of storage conditions including variations in temperature, vibration, humidity, and atmospheric pressure, and have a strong and compact, theft, and vandalism-proof packaging.

docs.title: User Story #1: Jenna
docs.text:
Jenna is a 33-year-old executive who regularly visits a bar for lunch to blow off some steam. The bar is often loud with people, but it is paramount that she can hold business conversations over the phone there. Then again, she does not want to miss out on the atmosphere and be able to hear the waiters as well. Her new Apple wireless earphones allow her to switch instantly between a mode where she can fully focus on the phone conversation and a mode where the phone call and environmental sound are seamlessly combined. They also allow her to rapidly adjust the volume on the earbuds themselves without having to take out her phone.

Jenna occasionally visits the bar in the evenings. She is a big fan of the L.A. Lakers, and whenever they play, she streams the live footage through her phone. Her new earbuds allow her to easily switch to hearing everything around her and streaming the match commentary without having to ever take the earbuds out. She sometimes gets compliments on how stylish the earbuds look on her, and she wouldn’t want to miss out on hearing those either.

docs.title: Aspects
docs.text:
The new product design will be based on that of the AirPods with improvements based on the following requirements. The P1 - P10 is the "code" to indicate the priority of the requirement, from low to high.

  1. Producer Design
  2. 1.1 The product shall be visually easy to distinguish from existing AirPods as well as main competitors Sony WF-1000XM3, Jabra Elite, Amazon Echo Buds, Samsung Galaxy Buds, and Bose SoundSport Free, and Urbanista Stockholm. (P10)
  3. 1.1 The product shall be easy to recognize as an Apple product without needing a logo on its exterior. (P10)

  4. 1.2. The product shall avoid styling elements from our Powerbeats over-ear wireless headphones since those address a different market segment. (P8)

  5. Functionality

    • 2.1 The product shall incorporate one or more optical proximity sensors to detect the user wearing it. (P10)
    • 2.2 The product shall offer a dual microphone in each earbud. (P10)

docs.title: Team Goals
docs.text:
Team 102 established the following shared goals for Project Aurora:

  1. Design and demonstrate a functional system that waters a small garden only when the soil requires water.
  2. Reduce unnecessary water use by using collected rainwater and stopping irrigation when the required soil-moisture level is reached.
  3. Protect the water pump from dry running, blocked tubing, and other unsafe operating conditions.
  4. Design four safe, modular PCBs that communicate reliably and operate together as one complete system.
  5. Give every team member practical experience with circuit design, PCB development, embedded programming, testing, and technical documentation.
  6. Maintain a fair workload, meet project deadlines, and produce professional work that team members can include in their engineering portfolios.

docs.title: Main Method for Group Communication
docs.text:
The team’s primary communication method will be group text messages. Text messages will be used for quick questions, meeting reminders, schedule updates, and urgent information.

Discord will be used for longer discussions and for organizing links, project files, design resources, and assignment materials. The team will also maintain the required shared Google Drive folder for master copies of documents and other project work. Email will be used for formal communication and instructor correspondence.

docs.title: Communication Procedures
docs.text:
The team will use group text messages for routine communication and Discord for detailed discussions and shared project materials. Team members are expected to respond within a reasonable amount of time and notify the group as early as possible if they cannot complete an assigned task or attend a meeting.

Sam Kholmuminov will serve as the liaison between the team and the instructor. When the team has a question or issue that requires instructor assistance, the members will explain it to Sam, and Sam will communicate it to the instructor. Sam will also share the instructor’s response with the entire team through the group message and Discord.

docs.title: Meeting Coordination
docs.text:
The team will create a shared calendar containing recurring meetings, assignment deadlines, design reviews, and other important project dates. Calendar notifications and group text messages will be used as meeting reminders.

If the team needs to add or change a meeting, members will discuss their availability through the group message and select a time that works for everyone. If a team member cannot attend a scheduled meeting, that person must notify the group as early as possible. The team will then decide whether to continue the meeting, reschedule it, or provide the absent member with notes and action items.

The preferred meeting format is face-to-face because it allows the team to work directly with project hardware and resolve design problems efficiently. Virtual meetings may be used when an in-person meeting is not practical. No additional meeting procedures are currently considered necessary, but the team may revise these procedures if communication problems develop.

docs.title: Roles & Responsibilities
docs.text:
Appendix Table 3: Project Roles and Duties

Role Duties Meeting leader Schedules team meetings, creates and distributes an agenda for each meeting, and runs each meeting Meeting recorder Takes minutes of each team meeting, including attendance, and records action items and to whom they are assigned Assignment leader Coordinates the team’s work on a given assignment and submits the completed assignment to Canvas before the deadline Project monitor Tracks the team’s progress relative to the project schedule and keeps team members informed of deadlines and project status

The initial roles are assigned as follows:

  • Natalia Castillo-Diaz — Meeting Leader: Schedules meetings, prepares and distributes agendas, and leads each meeting.
  • Arya Padiyar — Meeting Recorder: Records attendance, meeting notes, decisions, action items, responsible members, and completion dates.
  • Taylor Callo — Assignment Leader: Coordinates assignment completion, confirms that the required materials are ready, and submits assignments to Canvas on time.
  • Sam Kholmuminov — Project Monitor and Instructor Liaison: Tracks project progress, maintains the team’s GitHub repository, verifies that website updates are published, monitors deadlines, and communicates with the instructor when necessary.

Roles will be reviewed after each major assignment or project milestone. The team may rotate roles so that each member gains experience with different responsibilities. Assignments will be based on workload, availability, and the skills each member wants to develop.

Team members will assist one another when someone has difficulty completing a responsibility. If a role becomes too demanding or a member becomes unavailable, the team will discuss the situation and temporarily redistribute the work. Technical responsibilities for the four project subsystems will be assigned after the system requirements and component options are evaluated.

docs.title: Team Coordination & Accountability
docs.text:
The assignment leader will identify each upcoming deadline and help divide the required work among the team members. Whenever possible, individual contributions should be completed at least 48 hours before the Canvas deadline. The complete assignment will be shared with the team for review at least 24 hours before submission. Each member will review the work and confirm approval through the group message before the assignment leader submits it.

Sam will verify that the team’s GitHub repository and website contain the most recent approved content. Taylor will verify that the correct links and files are submitted to Canvas. Important project files will be maintained in the shared Google Drive folder, with links organized through Discord.

Team members will share technical information, explain their subsystem decisions, and help one another develop the skills required for each assignment. If a member needs additional support, the team may arrange a work session, divide the task into smaller steps, consult course resources, or ask the instructor for assistance.

Feedback from instructors and design reviews will be posted in Discord and discussed during the next team meeting. The team will create action items for each required revision and assign a responsible member and completion date.

A team member may be considered underperforming if there is a repeated pattern of missed meetings, incomplete assignments, limited communication, or failure to meet agreed-upon deadlines. The team will first contact the member privately, listen to the circumstances, and establish a reasonable improvement plan. If the problem continues, the entire team will discuss the issue and document the missed responsibilities. If no improvement occurs, Sam will bring the documented concern to the instructor and follow the course procedure, which may include a pink slip.

docs.title: Conflict Recognition & Resolution
docs.text:
The team recognizes that disagreements are normal during an engineering project. When a conflict occurs, the members involved will discuss the issue respectfully and focus on project requirements, available evidence, safety, cost, and user needs instead of personal opinions.

Both sides will be given an opportunity to explain their concerns. The team will attempt to identify common ground and select a solution that best supports the project mission. When possible, competing design ideas will be compared using calculations, testing, or a decision matrix.

If a member is causing a problem, missing responsibilities, or falling behind, the team will meet with that person privately. The purpose of the meeting will be to understand the situation, identify the required improvement, and agree on specific next steps. If the team cannot resolve the problem internally, Sam, as the instructor liaison, will explain the situation to the instructor and request assistance.
